pool.text: The port of Georgetown was founded as part of the territory.
Georgetown's Old Stone House was built as the oldest-standing building.
Georgetown University was founded featuring mixed architectural styles.
The Residence Act was adopted on July 16, approving capital creation.
Pierre Charles L'Enfant designed the city split into quadrants.
The United States Marine Band was founded near Capitol Hill.
The United States Supreme Court Building was completed.
The flag of Washington, D.C., was adopted as a coat of arms variation.
Arena Stage was founded, boosting the independent theater movement.
Ben's Chili Bowl was founded as a signature restaurant on U Street.
The district was granted presidential voting rights by the 23rd Amendment.
The Capital Beltway highway loop was constructed around the city region.
Washington, D.C., voted consistently for Democratic presidential candidates since receiving electoral votes.
Riots broke out in predominantly black residential and commercial corridors.
A restaurant rose to prominence during violent race riots in the city.
Congress enacted the Home Rule Act providing an elected mayor.
The Home Rule Act devolved certain Congressional powers to an elected mayor.
Metro opened and consists of six lines, 98 stations, and track.
The GALA Hispanic Theatre was founded in Columbia Heights.
The District of Columbia Voting Rights Amendment was passed by Congress.
